name: orlan
author: invented board game (lateral direction)
description:
INVENTED BOARD GAME (v3 - softened decisively after iterations 1 and 2).
Clue: a small position (5x5..6x6) drawn with '.' empty, 'o' your pieces, 'x' enemy pieces,
'#' immovable blocks. Answer: one move "r,c>r,c", 0-indexed row,col (the scorer accepts any
four integers in order).

HIDDEN RULES. (1) LEAP LENGTH: a piece's leap length n is the number of its four orthogonal
neighbours that hold a piece - 'o', 'x' or '#'. The board rim is NOT a neighbour. A piece
with n = 0 cannot move. (2) MOVE: it leaps exactly n squares in one of the four orthogonal
directions, flying over whatever lies between (empty squares and pieces alike); the landing
square must be on the board and empty. (3) You move an 'o'. (4) GOAL: after your move no
'x' may have a legal move under the very same rule.

The scorer is PROPERTY-BASED: it accepts ANY legal 'o' move that leaves every 'x'
immobile - it never compares against a reference answer. The generator simply arranges for
exactly one such move to exist on the whole board.

WHY v3 EXISTS. Iterations 1 and 2 both ended with two Opus teams PARTIAL at 23-32 % and
neither found the movement law. Each time they settled on a proxy law that my positives
never falsified: v1 winners landed on the first empty cell along their ray 67 % of the
time ("hop to the first empty cell"); v2 winners always leapt 2 or 3, so "exactly two
non-wall steps" and "the second empty cell" fitted 100 % of their confirmed answers. The
proxy was never contradicted, so nobody ever counted the mover's neighbours - and because
the goal reuses the law, the goal stayed invisible too.

v3 attacks that directly. The generator now picks the leap length per seed from
{1,2,3,4} (measured 32/32/25/11 %) and pads the origin with pieces until the mover's
neighbour count is exactly that, and it varies the flight path (all empty / all occupied).
The result, measured over 1500 fresh clues as "how often is the winning move even LEGAL
under this law" (a law that always contains the winner can never be falsified):

  TRUE  leap = #occupied orthogonal neighbours   100 %   (uniform pick among its moves: 16 %)
  first empty cell                                48 %   (2.4 %/uniform 4.2 %)
  second empty cell        (iteration 2 team b)   45 %
  k non-wall steps, walls transparent (team a)   <=41 %
  fixed distance k                               <=32 %
  slide with a clear path                         57 %
  leap = #occupied of all 8 neighbours            31 %
  leap = #adjacent pieces excluding blocks        21 %
  leap = #adjacent enemies                         8 %

Every proxy is now contradicted by 2-3 confirmed answers, and - the decisive change - the
true law is also the highest-scoring law by 2.5x (16 % vs <=6.5 % for any proxy), so the
score gradient finally points at the truth instead of away from it. In v2 the best proxy
outscored the true law, which is why both teams walked away from it.

Also softened: legal 'o' moves per clue reduced to 4-8 (mean 6.3), so knowing the law alone
is worth ~16 %; and generate() is 3x faster (mean 1.4 ms, max 8.6 ms over 3000 seeds), so a
0.5 s round presents ~350 clues instead of ~90 and the selection rule is within statistical
reach.

GENERATION is reverse: build a random position in which no 'x' can move (blocks are added
to repair mobile ones), un-move one 'o' by n squares, pad the origin until its neighbour
count is exactly n, then verify by enumeration: 4-8 legal 'o' moves, EXACTLY ONE of which
freezes every 'x', at least one 'x' currently mobile, and the winner is not the unique
longest, unique shortest, unique move landing nearest an enemy, only move landing beside an
enemy, only move whose mover touches an enemy, or only move that flies over a gap.

WITNESS LEAKS. Best constant answer 2 %. Best of 20 cheap selection heuristics 23.8 %
("the longest legal move" = "the mover with the most neighbours") - note that every one of
them already requires the movement law, so none of them is a shortcut past it. Uniform
guessing among legal moves 16.4 %.
